title: String Quartet No. 14 in D minor, “Death and the Maiden”
hook: Four players and one shadow, in a quartet built around Schubert’s song of Death coming for a young girl.

painting.title: Death and the Maiden
painting.pairingNote: Painted in Vienna under the same title, a girl clinging to a dark-robed figure of Death on a rumpled sheet, with the same mix of dread and tenderness as Schubert’s song.

facts: Schubert wrote it in March 1824, after a year of serious illness, poverty and failures. In a letter of that time he described himself as a man whose health would never return and whose brightest hopes had come to nothing.

The name comes from the second movement: [[variation|variation]]s on the piano part of his 1817 [[lied|lied]] “Der Tod und das Mädchen”. In Matthias Claudius’s poem a girl begs Death to pass her by, and Death answers gently that he comes as a friend.

It was first played in January 1826 at a private house in Vienna and published only in 1831, three years after Schubert’s death. The leading violinist Ignaz Schuppanzigh, the story goes, told him to stick to his songs.
A triplet rhythm runs through all four movements, and the finale is a [[tarantella|tarantella]], a whirling dance in 6/8.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a struggle (I), Death’s song and five variations (II), a fierce dance (III), a dance of death (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: A movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] that lurches between violence and tenderness. A short, hammering triplet figure from the first bar drives almost everything, even under the gentle second theme.

mainIdeas.name: The opening
mainIdeas.description: a loud [[unison|unison]] D and a hammering triplet figure, then a sudden, hushed [[chorale|chorale]].

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a quiet line over a restless ripple of triplets in the lower instruments.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, lilting tune for the two violins in thirds, in F major.

stops.hear: All four play one loud note, then a hammering triplet figure; suddenly very quiet chords
stops.happening: The introduction: the triplet motif and the first leap from loud to soft

stops.hear: Quiet and restless: a hushed line above, triplets rippling below
The two violins together, sweetly, in a lilting tune
The same tune, now with a stream of quick notes around it, wandering through keys
The gentle tune turned violent, loud, in a minor key
stops.happening: The [[exposition|exposition]] ends in an outburst, in A minor

stops.hear: The second theme, now soft, now furious, in turn
The triplet figure and the restless first theme return
The violins’ lilting tune, calmer, in the major
Soft, hymn-like chords; then the opening theme at a faster speed

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The rush breaks off; the triplet figure, slower again, dies away
stops.happening: A quiet ending in D minor

notice: Follow the triplet figure. It is in the opening bar, under the first theme, around the second, and it is the last thing you hear.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The Alban Berg Quartett do not repeat the exposition, so the movement lasts about 11½ minutes instead of about 15.

movements.heading: Andante con moto
movements.summary: A theme and five variations. The theme is the slow, solemn music of Death from Schubert’s song, played as quiet chords. Each variation keeps its shape and changes its character.

stops.hear: Slow, quiet chords for all four, like a solemn march
stops.happening: The theme, in G minor: Death’s music from the song. It ends on a major chord

stops.hear: The first violin floats a light line above the theme; the inner voices pulse in triplets
The cello sings the theme; the first violin flickers above in quick notes
Loud and galloping, then suddenly soft, with the first violin high above
G major, gentle; long triplet lines in the first violin over the melody below
stops.happening: Variation 4, the only one in the major

stops.hear: The second violin has the theme while the first violin races in quick arpeggios; the music swells, then fades
The theme returns, slower and quieter, in G major

notice: Listen to the last chords at the end of the theme (≈ 2:00) and of the whole movement. Death’s music ends in the major: comfort, not terror.

movements.heading: Scherzo. Allegro molto – Trio
movements.summary: A short, fierce [[scherzo|scherzo]] full of off-beat accents, and a [[trio|trio]] in D major that is the quartet’s only real moment of rest.

stops.hear: Fierce, stamping rhythms with accents off the beat; loud and soft collide
stops.happening: The scherzo, in D minor, with [[syncopation|syncopation]]

stops.hear: Slower and gentle: a warm tune in the lower voices, the first violin dancing above
The fierce rhythm again

movements.heading: Presto
movements.summary: A relentless [[tarantella|tarantella]] in [[rondo|rondo]] form: the main tune returns between other sections, and the speed only increases. A last, even faster rush ends in D minor.

mainIdeas.name: The main tune
mainIdeas.description: a galloping, limping dance in 6/8, first played by all four together.

mainIdeas.name: The second theme
mainIdeas.description: a broad, chorale-like melody in long notes; later the first violin runs in triplets around it.

stops.hear: All four together, a galloping, limping dance tune
stops.happening: The main theme of the tarantella

stops.hear: A broad, hymn-like melody in long notes
The galloping tune again
Swirling triplets and shifting accents; it is hard to feel where the beat is
The broad melody again
The galloping tune once more, growing louder
stops.happening: The last return of the main theme

stops.hear: Even faster; a burst of D major, then a turn back to D minor

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A furious dash to the last chords

notice: Listen for the moment at ≈ 8:15 when the music brightens into D major. It sounds like an escape, and it is taken away.

threads.title: The triplet
threads.body: A rhythm of three quick notes appears in every movement, from the first bar to the galloping finale.

threads.title: Loud against soft
threads.body: Sudden switches from *fortissimo* to *pianissimo* run through the whole quartet.

threads.title: Dances with death
threads.body: A death march in the variations, a fierce scherzo and a tarantella: Death’s music keeps turning into dance.
